key_insight: PEA spacers improve crystal morphology and suppress lattice defects, slowing ambient light- and heat-induced degradation compared with BA spacers in two-dimensional lead iodide perovskites.
engineering_relevance: Spacer selection offers a route to more stable perovskite devices but should complement surface passivation and encapsulation.
method: Compared BA₂PbI₄ and PEA₂PbI₄ perovskite nanoflakes.
Evaluated light and thermal stability under ambient conditions.
Probed degradation using confocal micro-Raman and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
evidence_signal: Freshly exfoliated samples showed comparable room-temperature luminescence, while PEA-based crystals degraded more slowly despite both materials losing organic components and decomposing into PbI₂ and metallic Pb.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative lifetime or device-efficiency results, so improved material stability should not be equated with demonstrated solar-cell durability.
paper_title: Impact of organic spacer cations on the light and thermal stability of two-dimensional lead halide perovskites
